AliceGoto/nighthawk.body:
# NightHawk

**A security-first AI agent for the terminal — penetration testing, code audit, and full-strength coding in one loop.**

NightHawk is built around a simple thesis: offensive security and serious engineering belong in the same agent. It pairs a modern coding agent core (Turn/Step loop, sub-agents, MCP, skills, persistent memory) with a native security engine — 116 vulnerability rules mapped to OWASP Top 10 and CWE, Shannon-entropy secret detection, cross-file taint analysis, and dependency auditing (offline, OSV, and host package-manager) — all exposed as first-class tools the agent can invoke mid-session.

[中文文档](https://github.com/AliceGoto/nighthawk/blob/HEAD/README.zh-CN.md)

---

## Why NightHawk

Most AI coding agents help you write code faster. NightHawk helps you **break it, prove it, and fix it**:

- **Audit as a first-class workflow.** Ask "audit this repo for injection risks" and the agent runs `SecurityScan`, triages findings by severity, confirms exploitability with `TaintTrace`, and proposes fixes — in one turn.
- **Offensive-security oriented.** Secret hunting, dependency risk, dangerous-sink tracing, and configuration flaws are surfaced by the same loop…

# Meowpick Backend

Meowpick is a course evaluation platform for WeChat mini programs. This repository provides backend APIs covering WeChat login, user profiles, course and teacher search, comments, likes, course addition proposals, admin approval, and operation logs.

## Tech Stack

- Go 1.25.5
- Gin
- MongoDB (Approval and withdrawal rely on transactions; must use replica sets or sharded clusters)
- Redis (Caching; MongoDB is the source of truth for business data and basic mapping)
- Google Wire
- Swagger / OpenAPI 3.1
- Docker

## Main Features

- WeChat mini program login and JWT Bearer authentication;
- User nickname, avatar, contribution points, and admin permission management;
- Course search by course name, teacher, department, category, and campus;
- Course comments, tags, likes, and personal comment history;
- Search history and suggestions for courses, teachers, departments, and categories;
- Users submit course addition proposals; admins approve, reject, or withdraw approval after modifying the final course;
- Proposal contribution points, contributor display, and admin operation logs;
- Department, course category, and campus mapping persisted to MongoDB, with Redis accelerating bidirectional queries.

## Directory Structure

```text
.
├── api/
│   ├── handler/          # HTTP parameter binding and responses
│   └── router/           # Route registration
├── application/
│   ├── assembler/        # Data model and DTO conversion
│   ├── dto/              # API request and response structures
│   └── service/          # Business logic
├── docs/                 # OpenAPI and design, migration documentation
├── infra/
│   ├── cache/            # Redis caching
│   ├── config/           # Configuration loading
│   ├── model/            # MongoDB models
│   ├── repo/             # Data access
│   └── util/             # Utility functions and runtime mapping
├── provider/             # Wire dependency injection
├── scripts/              # BSON migration orchestration scripts
└── types/                # Constants, error codes, and migration seed mapping
```

## Local Development

### Environment Requirements

- Go 1.25.5 or a compatible newer version;
- MongoDB replica set or sharded cluster; standalone cannot be used;
- Redis;
- WeChat mini program AppID and AppSecret required for production login. …

EEliberto/SurgeRelay-macOS.body:
# Surge Relay (macOS) " />

A macOS application for centralized management, conversion, editing, and publishing of Surge modules.

Built on the local conversion capabilities of Script-Hub.

Surge Relay is suitable for users who need to maintain a large number of Surge modules simultaneously, especially in scenarios where Loon, Quantumult X, or other proxy tool formats are frequently converted to Surge `.sgmodule` through Script-Hub. Its goal is to centralize module conversion, address maintenance, rule editing, and multi-device synchronization on a single Mac. You only need to maintain upstream addresses and conversion rules in Surge Relay, and the final Surge modules will be published to stable distribution addresses, with all devices only needing to subscribe to these fixed URLs. ## Preview

## Features ### 1. Centralized Module Management In the traditional workflow, if upstream authors change repository addresses, file paths, or directory structures, users typically need to reopen Script-Hub, reconvert modules, and reinstall them on Surge. For users with multiple devices, this process needs to be repeated on each device. Even with iCloud synchronization, it still requires multiple clicks to install, resulting in high maintenance costs. Surge Relay centralizes these workflows on a single Mac. You only need to maintain upstream addresses, backup addresses, and conversion rules in the app, while Surge devices don't need to worry about the original module sources.

### 2. Stable Module Distribution Addresses Surge Relay publishes processed Surge `.sgmodule` files to a private GitHub repository and provides stable addresses through Cloudflare; it can also be saved to a local iCloud Drive directory. Surge apps on all iPhones, iPads, Apple TVs, and Macs only need to subscribe to these fixed URLs. Even if upstream module addresses change, you only need to modify them once in Surge Relay. The subscription addresses on devices remain unchanged, without needing to reinstall modules or reconfigure each device individually.

### 3. Local Conversion and Automatic Publishing Surge Relay runs on your Mac, responsible for pulling upstream modules, invoking Script-Hub's local conversion logic, applying custom rules, and generating the final usable Surge modules. Generated modules can be automatically published to a private GitHub repository with Cloudflare, or saved to iCloud Drive (recommended). To prevent public repositories from being abused in bulk, Surge Relay does not allow public repositories as sync targets. The Mac is only responsible for building and publishing, while user devices read already-published stable files. Therefore, even if the Mac is shut down or temporarily unreachable, already-published modules continue to work normally. ####…

GOOFY-04/research-harness.body:
# research-harness

## One-Click Deployment

Execute one command in the repository root directory to create or reuse a Python virtual environment, install dependencies, create `.env`, clone or fast-forward update the private OpenCode fork, install Bun dependencies, run integration checks and start the research CLI:

```powershell
python deploy.py --start
```

Requires Python 3.10+, Git, and Bun to be pre-installed, and ensure Git has read access to the private repository `GOOFY-04/opencode`. The script will not overwrite existing `.env` files, and will not update `opencode-fork` with uncommitted changes. After the first deployment, fill in `AGNES_API_KEY` in `.env` to initiate model requests.

To deploy and validate without starting the CLI, execute `python deploy.py`. When network is limited and local dependencies are ready, you can use `--no-update`; use `--skip-checks` only when you explicitly need a quick reinstall. It is safe to run the deployment command repeatedly; OpenCode updates use `--ff-only` and will not automatically merge diverged history.

Deployment checks will run Python tests, research workbench type checking, Bash/PowerShell WASM parsing tests, and `--help` on the actual OpenCode startup entry point. Shell parsing uses WASM files from dependency packages; the fork no longer triggers compilation of unused native syntax bindings, avoiding path length errors on Windows deep directory installations.

Recoverable pipeline for long-horizon research: research planning, literature retrieval, method design, code generation and verification, review, paper drafting and project documentation.

See [2026-09-22 Validation Record](https://github.com/GOOFY-04/research-harness/blob/HEAD/docs/VALIDATION_20260922.md) for the latest tested results and known gaps, containing two complete runs that did not pass research acceptance with reproducible examples. Complete experiment configuration now requires [paired measurement contract](https://github.com/GOOFY-04/research-harness/blob/HEAD/docs/EXPERIMENT_CONTRACT.md): declare metric meanings and comparison scope before running; after running, the harness recalculates paired statistics from archived data. This check does not guarantee experimental design validity; real reviewer calibration still exposes issues in phrasing and research value judgments.

What runs by default is **code quick verification**, not complete training or research conclusion verification. Papers are based on actual execution logs; incomplete experiments should be clearly marked as TODO; final research conclusions still require real data, baseline comparisons and manual review.

## Installation

Requires Python 3.10+. A separate virtual environment is recommended; the following is for Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
python -m venv .venv…
```

Free Apple ID signing typically expires after 7 days. When the app won't open after expiration, reconnect the iPhone and press `Cmd + R` in Xcode to reinstall and renew the signing for 7 more days:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22
npx cap open ios
```

If you're only renewing the signing without changing content, you don't need to rebuild the web artifacts.

If you've modified the blog content, you need to rebuild and sync first:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview

MOBILE=1 npm run docs:build

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22.22.2

# 🪪 Hong Kong Immigration Department Appointment Quota Monitoring

Real-time tracking of Hong Kong Immigration Department **ID Card Replacement** appointment quotas, with automatic notifications via **Feishu Groups + Feishu Private Chat** when new quotas become available.

---

## 📱 Method 1: Join a Feishu Group (Recommended)

The bot automatically pushes quota changes, **instant message delivery**, join the group and use immediately, no configuration needed.

> 📖 **[Group Information & How to Join](https://scn7uo58gnuo.feishu.cn/wiki/QSFlwcMBmil7sGkZRBTcAWqwnCf)** (Multiple group options, automatic distribution when groups are full)

### 💬 Method 2: Feishu Private Chat Subscription

If you don't want to join a group, you can also **filter by date**, receiving notifications only for the dates you care about:

1. [Private chat with the bot "HKID Quota Automatic Monitoring"](https://applink.feishu.cn/T98uc8RbxI8c) (Send any message to trigger)
2. The bot will respond with an interactive card supporting:
   - 📅 **Subscribe to Specific Dates** — Focus only on your appointment date
   - 🔔 **Subscribe to All Dates** — Receive notifications for all quota releases
   - 📊 **View / Modify / Cancel Subscription**
3. You can also reply directly with dates for one-click subscription, e.g., `08/15, 08/20-08/25`

Three filtering modes are supported:
- 📅 **By Date** — View only specific dates, all locations
- 🏢 **By Location** — View only specific locations, all dates
- 🎯 **By Date + Location** — Exact matching

> 💡 The bot private chat has a 1-2 second delay; if you're in a hurry, joining the group is recommended.

---

## 🖥 Dashboard

> 🖥 **[quota-monitor Dashboard](https://Zheyi-D.github.io/quota-monitor)**

- 📊 Real-time view of appointment quota status for all locations across Hong Kong
- 📈 Quota release pattern heatmap, visualizing release frequency by time period
- 📖 Includes telephone appointment tutorial
- 🔧 Built-in admin backend, supports subscriber management, statistics overview, dual-channel group messaging

---

## 📨 Notification Flow

When new quotas are detected, notifications are pushed in the following order:

> **Group Broadcast** (parallel across multiple groups) → **Private Message DM** (parallel, only sent to subscribers matching the date)

Feishu group and private messages arrive almost simultaneously.

---

## 🔒 Privacy & Security

- Feishu user data is stored with **AES-256-GCM encryption**, unreadable in the repository
- Only reads quota data **publicly published** by the Immigration Department
- ⚠️ Disclaimer: This system is a third-party open-source tool, not an official service of the Hong Kong Immigration Department, please refer to the official website for accurate information

# Enterprise Knowledge Base Advanced RAG Intelligent Q&A System

An enterprise knowledge base Q&A platform based on Vue 3 + FastAPI. The project supports login authentication, knowledge base management, file upload and parsing, multi-knowledge base isolated retrieval, image attachment Q&A, SSE streaming responses, multi-turn conversation memory, and RAGAS online evaluation.

## 1. Architecture Overview

### Overall Architecture

```text
Vue 3 Frontend
  -> Pinia / Vue Router / Element Plus
  -> Fetch SSE call /api/chat/stream
  -> FastAPI routing layer
  -> JWT authentication and user context parsing
  -> Conversation memory / image understanding / RAG routing decision
  -> retrieve_knowledge retrieval chain
  -> DeepSeek / DashScope / Milvus / MySQL
  -> SSE stream responses with answers, sources, Trace, and completion events
```

### Backend Layering

```text
backend/
  router/       API route mounting, responsible for routing HTTP requests to service
  service/      Business orchestration, such as chat flow, knowledge base upload, deletion rollback
  rag/          RAG core capabilities: LLM, Milvus, rerank, memory, Trace, RAGAS, vision understanding
  database/     SQLAlchemy Session, MySQL initialization, checkpointer
  model/        ORM data models
  schema/       Pydantic request and response structures
  crud/         Data access logic
```

### Frontend Layering

```text
src/
  api/          Axios / Fetch API wrapper, including streamChat
  stores/       Pinia state management
  views/        Chat, Knowledge, Login, Profile pages
  components/   Markdown, Trace, general display components
  utils/        SSE parsing, file validation, date formatting, and other utilities
```

### Data and Retrieval Architecture

- MySQL stores users, conversations, messages, knowledge bases, file metadata, and evaluation results.
- Milvus / Milvus Lite stores document chunk vectors, using `knowledge_base_id` for multi-knowledge base isolation.
- When uploading files, file validation, text extraction, and semantic chunking are performed first, then written to MySQL and Milvus; rollback is executed on failure.
- When deleting a knowledge base or file, corresponding SQL records and vector data are cleaned up to keep metadata and vector indices consistent.

# EX

> A personalized content community built with Go + Vue, centered around recommendation systems, asynchronous event processing, and data consistency.

EX connects content publishing, social interaction, behavior collection, and personalized recommendations into a complete product workflow: users publish short-form or long-form posts, generating feedback through following, liking, replying, and reading. The backend projects this feedback into behavioral data and interest profiles, providing recommendation signals for subsequent Feed requests.

The project's engineering focus is on **the recommendation pipeline and state consistency of the Go backend**, while providing Vue 3 frontend, containerized development environment, automated testing, and observability capabilities.

[Technical Design](#technical-design) · [System Architecture](#system-architecture) · [Quick Start](#quick-start) · [Testing and Verification](#testing-and-verification) · [Project Structure](#project-structure)

## Project Overview

| Aspect | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Personalized Recommendation | Four-source recall, Equal RRF candidate fusion, positive/negative interest vectors, multi-signal ranking, diversity and exploration |
| Asynchronous Consistency | Redis Lua atomic operations, versioned like snapshots, transactional Outbox, Debezium CDC, Consumer Inbox deduplication |
| Content and Social | Unified Post model, short-form and long-form posts, replies and quotes, retweets, following, notifications, cursor-based pagination |
| Full-stack Interaction | Feed and detail page data linkage, cross-page interaction sync, account identity isolation, reading behavior collection |
| Engineering Foundation | API / Worker role-based execution, independent migrations, health checks, Prometheus / Grafana, layered CI |

## Product Features

chen1111-a/hkid-quota-monitor.body:
# Hong Kong ID Card Appointment Quota Dashboard

Monitor the smart ID card appointment quota of the Hong Kong Immigration Department's six registration offices, with detection approximately every 2 minutes. When quotas are released, subscribers are reminded via email/Feishu group. **Third-party public welfare tool, not an official Immigration Department service; only provides monitoring and reminders, does not perform any proxy booking or appointment.**

## Dashboard Entry Points

- **Preferred (stable direct connection within mainland China)**: https://hkid-quota-monitor.pages.dev/
- Backup: https://chen1111-a.github.io/hkid-quota-monitor/
  (Mainland China network access to github.io is intermittent; jsDelivr/raw direct links with nosniff headers will only display source code, do not use as web entry point)
- For complete experience within mainland China without VPN, use **email subscription + Feishu group** — notification path is entirely domestic direct connection, releases are pushed to phone immediately, dashboard is auxiliary only

## How It Works

```
cron-job.org (every 2 minutes) ──▶ GitHub Actions
                            │  python -m quota_monitor.run
                            │  ├─ Fetch Immigration Department public quota API (read-only, one request per cycle)
                            │  ├─ Diff with previous snapshot → quota release events
                            │  └─ commit data/ + refresh jsDelivr cache
                            ▼
        index.html dashboard (mobile-first, auto-refresh every 90 seconds)
        Email + Feishu notifications (triggered by quota release events, with debounce cooldown)
```

- API structure: [docs/api-notes.md](https://github.com/chen1111-a/hkid-quota-monitor/blob/HEAD/docs/api-notes.md)
- 2-minute trigger configuration: [docs/cron-setup.md](https://github.com/chen1111-a/hkid-quota-monitor/blob/HEAD/docs/cron-setup.md)

## Improvements Compared to Similar Tools

- **Mobile-first**: Dates scroll vertically, all 6 offices fit on one screen, no horizontal scrolling
- **Colorblind-friendly**: Status cells use color + text dual channel (available/limited/full)
- **Anti-notification spam**: Official API has load balancing data jitter (tested 304↔346 fluctuations within same minute), notification layer has per-slot cooldown period, won't spam every cycle
- **Mainland China direct connection**: Email subscription and Feishu notification paths are entirely domestic direct connection, no VPN required

falseeeeeeeeee/ShaderLibrary.body:
# 【ShaderLibrary】

[TOC]

------

# 😉Conventions

In Unity, there are three visual editors: [**Shader Forge (SF)**](https://www.acegikmo.com/shaderforge/), [**Amplify Shader Editor (ASE)**](http://amplify.pt/unity/amplify-shader-editor/), and [**Shader Graph (SG)**](https://docs.unity3d.com/cn/Packages/com.unity.shadergraph@10.5/manual/index.html). Although the code syntax is all [**ShaderLab**](https://docs.unity3d.com/cn/current/Manual/SL-Reference.html), it is mainly divided into two types: [**CG**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cg_%28programming_language%29) and [**HLSL**](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3dhlsl/dx-graphics-hlsl). Therefore, I am establishing my personal usage conventions here.

Since NVIDIA no longer updates the CG language and Unity is gradually abandoning it, with mobile devices becoming mainstream, most Shaders are written using the [**URP**](https://docs.unity3d.com/cn/Packages/com.unity.render-pipelines.universal@12.1/manual/index.html) pipeline. This project is based on [**URP 2021.3.0f1c1 and above**](https://unity.cn/releases/lts). I prefer to upgrade to newer versions and try not to maintain backward compatibility with older versions. Let's not keep riding the ship of the old era. If new things aren't good, then why does everyone spend time, effort, and money updating these things?

Naming prefixes follow the tool type used to create the Shader as a prefix. For example: ASE_XXX, SG_XXX...

Shader paths are classified according to the pipeline used, with the first level being the pipeline type and the second level being the category. For example: Default/Base/ASE_XXX, URP/Base/SG_XXX...

Shaders adopt a modular path structure, with each Shader in a separate folder. Related model materials and references are placed in the **ShaderLib** folder in the root directory. For example: Assets/ShaderLib/Base_XXX/S_XXX.shader

## Naming

| Tool Used                      | Prefix Abbreviation | Naming Format: Prefix Abbreviation_Name.xxx    |

ling-kong-ran/pisper.body:
Multi-Agent Application across Desktop, Terminal, and Mobile: Manage Agents like managing code branches - branch out from any completed Turn, advance in parallel.

## ✨ Why Pisper

- **Conversations can branch too.** Derive new sessions from any completed Turn, inherit context, source session remains unchanged; stable Turn labels pin key nodes into searchable anchors -- like Git, but for Agents.
- **True parallel multi-Agent.** Each session has its own model, context, working directory, and permissions; drag labels for four-way split-screen, progress visible on screen.
- **Tools with clear hot/cold distinction.** Core tools reside in context permanently; plugins, MCP, and skills are activated on-demand via discover/call gateway, withdrawn after use -- no matter how rich the capabilities, context won't become a junk room.
- **Stable prefix, hot cache.** Tool definitions stabilized and sorted, prompt form hash diagnosis, maximize Provider's prompt cache usage -- longer sessions faster and more economical.
- **Missing any capability? Say it directly.** Pisper writes, validates, and installs local plugins by itself, next conversation can call them.
- **Mobile independent or connected to desktop.** Android/iOS App has built-in Node/Pisper Runtime and React interface identical to desktop source, and closes unavailable entries based on actual device capabilities; can also scan code to connect to desktop, prioritize LAN, automatically fall back to Iroh P2P when leaving local network. Remote link continues using TLS fingerprint and device Bearer token.
- **Data stays on-device by default.** Runtime only listens to 127.0.0.1 by default, sensitive formats auto-desensitized, memory reviewed before use -- your context, you decide.

# 📡 Bilibili/Douyin Live Monitoring + Multi-channel Push

A lightweight live stream status monitoring tool that supports Bilibili and Douyin platforms, automatically sends notifications through multiple channels (Bark / Server-chan / WeChat Work / PushPlus / Telegram) when streaming starts / new works are published.

## ✨ Features

- 🎬 **Multi-platform support**: Monitor Bilibili and Douyin live rooms simultaneously
- 🔔 **Multi-channel push**: Send notifications through Bark / Server-chan / WeChat Work / PushPlus / Telegram when streaming starts / new works are published
- 📊 **Live duration statistics**: Record streaming duration, last streaming time
- 📝 **Historical logs**: Keep the last 200 status change records
- 🔄 **Merged push**: Combine multiple streamers' broadcasts into one notification when they go live simultaneously
- 📱 **Responsive pages**: Mobile-friendly monitoring interface
- 🎵 **New works detection**: Support detection of Douyin new works publication (optional)

## 📋 Quick Start

### 1. Configure monitored rooms

Edit the `rooms.json` file and add the streamers you want to monitor:

```json
[
  {
    "platform": "bilibili",
    "id": "1874913653",
    "name": "峰哥亡命天涯"
  },
  {
    "platform": "douyin",
    "id": "83134194400",
    "name": "27～"
  }
]
```

**Field descriptions:**
- `platform`: Platform, `bilibili` or `douyin`
- `id`: Live room ID
  - Bilibili: Live room number (the number in the URL, such as `https://live.bilibili.com/1874913653`)
  - Douyin: Live room web_rid (the string in the URL, such as `https://live.douyin.com/83134194400`)
- `name`: Streamer name (used for display and push notifications)

### 2. Configure push channels (optional)

Streaming / new works notifications support multiple channels, configured via environment variable `BLIVE_CONFIG` (JSON):

```bash
# Bark (iPhone, recommended)
export BLIVE_CONFIG='{"push": {"type": "bark", "url": "https://api.day.app/YOUR_KEY", "group": "blive"}}'

# or WeChat Work group bot (unlimited free, recommended)
export BLIVE_CONFIG='{"push": {"type": "wecom", "webhook": "https://qyapi.weixin.qq.com/cgi-bin/webhook/send?key=xxxx"}}'

# NewsNook（有所闻）

A local-first, out-of-the-box, freely extensible information aggregation and reading platform.

News, RSS, Web / CMS sites and independent content communities converge in a clean, controllable reading experience.

---

## What is NewsNook

NewsNook（有所闻）is neither a single RSS reader nor a traditional news client.

It aspires to become **a user's own information gateway**: after installation, you can read built-in news and topics, and you can also add your own RSS / Atom / JSON Feed, integrate recognizable Web / CMS directory sites, and use content communities like Zhihu through independent site workspaces.

These different sources ultimately converge into a unified set of reading capabilities: full-text reading, images and videos, translation, AI speed reading, read later, history, local search, offline caching, sharing and optional sync.

> NewsNook does not produce or host news content, nor does it drive content distribution through ads, cloud profiling, or engagement time.
> You decide what to read; the app takes responsibility for organizing content well, presenting it smoothly, and saving it to your own device.

### At a Glance

| Capability | NewsNook |
| --- | --- |
| Read immediately after installation | Built-in news sources, topic categories and scenario presets |
| Custom subscriptions | RSS 2.0 / Atom / RDF / JSON Feed / OPML |
| Web sites | Generic directory extraction and framework recognition |
| CMS | MacCMS, WordPress, Hugo, Hexo, Ghost, etc. |
| Independent site workspaces | Currently includes Zhihu workspace |
| Full text | Full text on-site, Readability and custom site extraction |
| Multimedia | Images, audio, Progressive / HLS / DASH, custom players |
| Screen casting | DLNA |
| Translation | Cloud translation, AI translation, Android local translation, Bergamot |
| AI | OpenAI-compatible Provider, AI speed reading |
| Local capabilities | Read later, history, search, recommendations, caching, reading position |
| Sync | Optional account, config-only sync; reading data remains local |
| Current main platform | Android |

---

## Why NewsNook

Today's information is typically scattered across news sites, RSS, blogs, independent websites, content communities, and video pages. The problem often isn't "lack of content," but rather the need to constantly switch between numerous apps, web pages, and algorithmic information feeds.

NewsNook attempts to provide another way.

No need to find RSS addresses on first installation.

The project includes built-in sources and scenario presets for news, technology, AI, business, international, and in-depth reading, which you can read immediately; you can then gradually adjust it to your own information structure.

z114880/everything-agent.body:
# Everything Agent

## Quick Start

Environment requirements: Node.js 24.12 or higher. The backend runs `src/` directly through Node.js native TypeScript type erasure, while the frontend is still handled by Vite. Memory uses Node.js built-in `node:sqlite`, and verifies FTS5 availability on startup; Session and Semantic FTS share nodejieba Chinese search tokenization, identifier whole-word and constituent-word indexing.

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run dev:web
```

`pnpm run dev:web` is the main command to start Everything Agent local console, Engine and Agent bridge interface. After startup, open the local address in your browser according to terminal output, and enter the "Configuration" page to set up your model.

Before submitting changes, you can run full checks and examples:

```bash
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm run example
```

When you need a batch of local test data, you can use a mock model to drive the real Runtime to generate and merge into the existing data directory, without consuming model quota or requiring internet:

```bash
pnpm run mock-data
```

Data is merged into `.everything/` by default, previously written datasets will not be rewritten, model configuration and vector indexing are unaffected; see [`mock-data/README.md`](https://github.com/z114880/everything-agent/blob/HEAD/mock-data/README.md) for details.

## Langfuse Production Environment Evaluation

```bash
pnpm run langfuse:up
pnpm run dev:web
```

The complete Docker Compose starts Langfuse v4 with database, object storage and experiment callback gateway, automatically generating local credentials on first run. The management platform address is `http://localhost:3300`, credentials are in `.langfuse/compose.env`. See [one-click deployment guide](https://github.com/z114880/everything-agent/blob/HEAD/deploy/langfuse/README.md) for details.

New **Evaluation** page supports launching real Agent from local or Langfuse Custom Experiment, using independent evaluation sessions, optional daily memory snapshots configured uniformly by Langfuse dataset metadata.memorySnapshot, real models and tools, retaining tool approval and cancellation capabilities; displays progress, results, usage, platform scores and sync errors. Use cases default to maximum 3 concurrent, configurable via backend environment variables…
